title: Evidence Package (EP-v1) (v2.9)
description: Evidence Package composed by the SENDER-SIDE RDP, always (D2/F-13; TS clause 4.1 — the former third-party EP-authority delegation is removed; the EP signer is bound to se.rdp_id in the trust store, LINT-TRUST-02/CF-6). Bundles SE with the final outcomes and records the RDP relay chain. On the wire the EP is a sealed evidence artefact `[cose-sign1, qualified-timestamp]` (this schema validates the PROJECTION, which carries no seal field); the artefact's qualified timestamp imprints SHA-256 of its first element (the EP COSE_Sign1) per the I-D (Evidence Objects and COSE Packaging) sequencing, attesting the time of bundle composition — which is the COMPOSER's act instant: the sender-side RDP (`se.rdp_id`) MUST be admitted to the federation at that instant, separately from the recorded acts inside the package, each checked at its own (R10-X5; umbrella §13.1); per-event legal times remain on the enclosed SE/DE/NDE/RE objects (the I-D (Evidence Objects and COSE Packaging), EPTS-1).

outcomes.description: The message's outcome evidence. A monotone finality rule (R1/R4, twenty-fourth review): each of DE-v1 (delivery), NDE-v1 (non-delivery) and RE-v1 (refusal) is a TERMINAL outcome, and an EP MUST carry at most ONE terminal outcome for its message (per grade where grades differ) — a DE and a terminal NDE/RE for the same message are contradictory. Retries are idempotent (I-D Error Handling and Retries); late or additional events are SUPPLEMENTARY evidence carried in `changes`/`states`, never replacing the terminal result. At-most-one-terminal is evidence_lint LINT-EP-07; the full state machine is normative in the I-D.

rdp_id.description: R8-05: declared an unconstrained string, so this evidence field admitted provider identifiers the rest of the model rejects.

evidence.description: OPTIONAL per-hop reference to this hop's sealed B.x relay evidence (RelayEvidence-v1), for the profile-2 four-corner case (FC-2; TS clause 4.1). Binds the specific relay-evidence object by the digest of its seal (see seal_digest for the exact input), so every hop is independently verifiable in a dispute (TS clause 4.1 dispute chain) rather than coupled to the archive by message_id convention alone. Absent in single-provider (profile-1) EPs. Its message_id equals the EP message_id (evidence_lint LINT-EP-06); where the referenced object is in the same bundle, the digest is recomputed and compared (bundle_lint LINT-BND-20).

seal_digest.description: The digest that binds this hop to its relay-evidence object. INPUT (normative, TS clause 4.1): the FIRST ELEMENT of the referenced object's evidence artefact — the exact serialized COSE_Sign1 octets — hex = lowercase-hex(SHA-256(cose-sign1)). NOT the base64 text: both are readings of 'the SHA-256 of its seal' and they yield DIFFERENT digests, so the input is fixed here. The decoded bytes are the profile's one convention — the qualified-timestamp imprint (LINT-PKG-08) digests the same input, so a seal has exactly one digest. `alg` names the hash FUNCTION; this description names its INPUT. Single implementation: lint_cli.compute_seal_digest; recomputed by bundle_lint LINT-BND-20; pinned in bytes by sample-EP-federated.json.

hex.description: lowercase-hex(SHA-256(cose-sign1)) over the referenced RelayEvidence-v1 artefact's first element (its serialized COSE_Sign1).

changes.description: Optional. Change-indication evidence (CE-v1) for any envelope/metadata transformation performed during sending or receiving (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, Article 44(1)(e)).

states.description: Optional. Non-DE, non-operative STATE RECORDS for states S1/S2/S3 (the I-D (Message Flows and Delivery States)): auditable metadata derived from authenticated MSP signals, NOT individually sealed and carrying no Article 43(2) effect; S1/S2 do not establish delivery. Each element records a state and its mapped EN 319 522-1 event and MUST NOT carry any delivery-establishing field (LINT-EP-04). Legally operative facts live in the sealed evidence objects.

disputes.description: OPTIONAL (X-04/D5, evidence 2.2): grade-commitment-mismatch dispute evidence (GCM-v1), embedded as sub-artefact bytes on the wire like outcomes/changes. A valid GCM REBUTS the availability DE in dispute; it is NOT a terminal outcome (LINT-EP-07 finality untouched) and never retracts the DE.
